newsitem.title: USA: FedEx says stretched to holiday levels.
newsitem.headline: FedEx says stretched to holiday levels.

text.p: The Teamsters strike at United Parcel Service of America Inc has caused an influx of business at rival Federal Express Corp, which has seen its package volume jump to nearly peak holiday levels.
"The system is challenged and stretched beyond normal capacity. We're approaching holiday-level capacity," said Jess Bunn, a Federal Express spokesman.
Federal Express said its volume in the U.S. has increased to about 3.5 to 4.0 million packages a day, compared to normal August volume of about 2.8 million.

Bunn said Memphis-based Federal Express has added additional crews and equipment to handle the jump in package volume. Federal Express said it is using its present workforce of 130,000 employees and has not added any temporary workers.
"We've had people cancel vacation time, stay over-time. We've had pilots offering to work extra. We've met the challenge," Bunn said.
Federal Express said it suspended its money-back guarantee on Friday and will not reinstate the offer until the UPS strike is over.
"We'll delivery it as best as possible, we're still working to provide time-definite reliability, but we're telling people that the money-back guarantee is not in effect," Bunn said.
Shares of Federal Express gained 15/16 to 64-5/8.
A nation-wide strike against UPS entered its second day on Tuesday with no talks scheduled between management and the Teamsters union representing UPS workers.

Operations at UPS, the nation's largest package delivery service, were paralyzed as 185,000 workers walked off their jobs after last-ditch contract talks between the company and the International Brotherhood of Teamsters broke down late Sunday.
